artefact_status: DECLARED-UNFITTED — a declared-coefficient parametric instance of the power_model/0 schema. No fit has run; no independence unit is scored; every coefficient value is a declared default anchored to a cited source, pending T1. Any figure derived from this artefact carries the DECLARED-UNFITTED label structurally, and any SVRR rendered from it must say so.

terms.name: calm_water_baseline
terms.coefficient_source: declared — admiralty-coefficient form is the canon standard (SNAME, Principles of Naval Architecture; MAN Energy Solutions, Basic Principles of Ship Propulsion, 2018); the C VALUE is a declared default pending the T1 fit, not taken from any single vessel

terms.name: windage_raa
terms.form: R_aa = 0.5 * rho_air * A_w(loading) * V_rel^2 * C_X(theta_rel), emitted as power at ship speed
terms.coefficient_source: declared — C_X per vessel type/loading from Blendermann (1994): head-wind anchors from the standard head-wind table, angular variation from the full tabulated curves reproduced in Dale (2020) Appendix E (see references and windage_cx_angular); pairs without a tabulated curve stay head-wind-only; Fujiwara regression remains T1 work for those pairs
terms.sign_convention: along-track signed: headwind penalty, following credit (C_X < 0 near theta = 180 flows through the same formula, no special-casing); lateral via induced resistance + steering drag (skeleton section 2, T1)
terms.sourced_coverage: theta_rel in [0, 180] (port/starboard symmetric, |theta| used) for container_ship|laden, cargo_vessel|laden, tanker|laden — linear interpolation between tabulated 10-degree points, declared; tanker|ballast and cargo_vessel|container_on_deck remain head-wind only (no tabulated curve exists in the source appendix) and refuse off-axis; |theta| > 180 refuses

terms.name: hull_degradation_t5
terms.form: interface only — monotone drift rate with provenance (skeleton section 2, T5)
terms.coefficient_source: none — T2's measurement; this instance declares the interface and carries no value

fit.method: none — declared parametric instance; no fit has run. The fit method is named at fit time per G8; the split is declared per G1

split.rule: none — nothing is scored by this artefact; the G1 split rule is declared at T1 fit time

coverage.unit: none — no independence unit is scored by this declared instance

admiralty_c.source: declared default pending T1 — published admiralty coefficients cluster roughly 400-700 depending on units convention (SNAME PNA; MAN Basic Principles 2018); the form is canon, the value is a placeholder the T1 fit replaces

rho_air.source: ISA sea-level standard atmosphere, declared constant (not fitted, not varied)

container_ship|laden.source: Blendermann (1994) head-wind C_X table, as reproduced in the NTNU thesis appendix (2021) and ITTC-referenced compilations

cargo_vessel|laden.source: Blendermann (1994) head-wind C_X table (cargo vessel, loaded)

cargo_vessel|container_on_deck.source: Blendermann (1994) head-wind C_X table (cargo vessel, container on deck)

tanker|ballast.source: Blendermann (1994) head-wind C_X table (tanker, ballast) — the loading-condition split the owner's ruling requires: ballast carries MORE windage area, and the table reflects it

metadata.source: Blendermann (1994) angular C_X tables, as tabulated in Dale (2020) Appendix E Tables E.2/E.3/E.4 — the appendix presents -C_X per its own preamble; values here are converted (C_X = -(tabulated)), so C_X > 0 is resistance and C_X < 0 is the following-wind credit. C_X is referenced to the frontal projected area at all angles (Blendermann 1994 convention), q on the apparent wind
metadata.extraction_record: corpus_intake/raw/windage_src/blendermann1994_angular_cx_extraction.json — retrieval path (search-indexed full text; PDF locked post-NVA-migration), raw tabulated values, and the theta=0 cross-validation gate
metadata.interpolation: linear between tabulated 10-degree points, declared; curves symmetric in port/starboard so |theta| is used; |theta| > 180 refuses
metadata.coverage_limit: no tanker-ballast and no cargo-with-containers curve exists in Dale (2020) Appendix E (E.1-E.9) — those pairs stay head-wind-only; Fujiwara (1998/2001) is the declared T1 extension for them

container_ship|laden.source: Blendermann (1994) container vessel curve, Dale (2020) Appendix E Table E.2

tanker|laden.source: Blendermann (1994) tanker (loaded) curve, Dale (2020) Appendix E Table E.3

cargo_vessel|laden.source: Blendermann (1994) cargo vessel curve, Dale (2020) Appendix E Table E.4

deliberate_exclusions.angular_windage_uncovered_pairs: angular C_X is carried ONLY for container_ship|laden, tanker|laden, cargo_vessel|laden (Dale 2020 Appendix E). tanker|ballast and cargo_vessel|container_on_deck have no tabulated curve in that source — they remain head-wind-only and refuse off-axis; the Fujiwara regression (1998/2001, ISO 15016-recommended) is the declared T1 extraction work for them
deliberate_exclusions.engine_efficiency_chain: no specific-consumption coefficient is carried anywhere in this artefact — power-to-consumables conversion is the denomination layer's domain (D1 ConversionFactor with its own provenance), per G7. Verified anchor for D1 when it needs it: MAN project-guide convention, g/kWh at ISO conditions on LCV 42,700 kJ/kg with 5% tolerance (e.g. MAN 5S35ME-B9.5: 173.0 g/kWh at SMCR, per the 2026 sea-trial literature)
deliberate_exclusions.waves_current: no wave or current term is carried — the Copernicus covariate hooks are T1/T2 intake work; declaring a form without a sourced coefficient would be the failure class this schema exists to block
